subject: Site queue surge causing 504s / timeouts — executive update requested
messages:
From: Samuel James <samuel.james@atlasretail.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Cc: katie.lin@atlasretail.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:12:03 -0500
Subject: Elevated 504s and timeouts impacting checkout - URGENT

Hi team,

We started seeing ~40% of checkout requests return 504/timeouts around 07:45 EST. Latency for remaining requests has spiked to 3-5s and we're hitting a ton of frontend retries which is making the situation worse. This is impacting our Black Friday-style promotion (traffic ~5x baseline). Please advise immediate mitigation steps — our ops lead is on standby and this is customer-impacting.

I've attached a small set of client-side traces and a screenshot of our dashboard.

Samuel
Ops Lead, Atlas Retail
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:20:11 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Elevated 504s and timeouts impacting checkout - URGENT

Marissa — can you triage? Initial ask: 1) confirm whether this is our side (routing, batching, KV cache) 2) immediate mitigation (fallback model / disable batching / route to dedicated) 3) ETA to a customer-facing note.

Vanessa / Grace — please standby for customer comms / exec outreach if needed.

I'll join the call in 10.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Account Execs | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:33:50 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Elevated 504s and timeouts impacting checkout - URGENT

Triage notes (initial):
- Symptoms: sharp growth in request queue length on serving pool for model: text-gen-4k-q4f. Concurrent queued requests exceed async batch window -> request timeouts and cascading retries.
- Probable cause: a recent batching optimization (defer-window=8ms) + an aggressive KV cache LRU tweak led to cache thrash on long-prefix traffic patterns. When cache hit rate drops, per-request latency rises and batching queues grow beyond SLOs.
- Evidence: distributed traces show large KV cache miss spikes at 07:43-07:50 (attached), head-of-line latency shards spiking to 12s, and number of inflight per-GPU requests doubled.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now (ordered):
1) Flip batching defer-window back to 4ms for this pool (rollback change pushed pipeline id: cfg-20270110-batch).
2) Pin serving pool to the 8x-large instance group that has a warmer KV cache (route traffic there).
3) Apply temporary response-throttling at the ingest edge to prevent client retry amplification (10rps burst cap per token).
4) If we can't drop latency in 10m, fallback Atlas to a smaller-generation model variant with lower KV dependency.

I'm pushing the rollback now and uploading traces (prod-traces-20270112.zip). ETA: 7-12m for rollback to take effect and for metrics to stabilize.

—Marissa
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samuel James <samuel.james@atlasretail.com>, Katie Lin <katie.lin@atlasretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:42:09 -0500
Subject: RE: Elevated 504s and timeouts impacting checkout - URGENT

Samuel / Katie — thank you for the quick report and apologies for the disruption. Our SRE has started immediate mitigations (rolling back a batching change and applying edge throttles). We expect to see improvement within ~10–15 minutes and I'll update you as soon as we have stabilization metrics.

Action items for Atlas: please keep retries limited on the client side while we stabilize (disable aggressive client-side retry for 30 minutes). We'll consider a goodwill credit if this impacts revenue.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Account Execs | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samuel James <samuel.james@atlasretail.com>, Katie Lin <katie.lin@atlasretail.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:05:34 -0500
Subject: Update: mitigation in progress + exec escalation

Hi Samuel / Katie,

Quick update: Marissa rolled back the recent batching tweak and we have throttled client-side retries at the edge. We're seeing queue depth decline and 504s drop from ~40% to ~8% over the last 12 minutes. Full stabilization is ongoing — I'll provide a dashboard snapshot in 30 minutes.

Separately, I want to escalate this to our leadership team to ensure you have an executive contact and to discuss credits and follow-up actions post-stabilization. We take this seriously and will share a full postmortem that includes root cause, mitigations, and a plan to prevent recurrence (config gating + canary policy).

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 13:45:00 -0500
Subject: Post-stabilization next steps (rollback + PM)

Team — final update from infra: metrics have stabilized ~3 hours after the incident window with 504s back to baseline and no further retry storms. We did a full rollback of the deploys touching batching and reverted the KV LRU tweak on the affected pools.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: run forensic on whether LRU thresholds + traffic shape could have been caught by canary (JIRA-3456) — due 2027-01-19
- Product: add canary gating for batching config changes (Vanessa) — due 2027-02-02
- CS/Acct (Grace/Karthik): customer exec outreach + formal credit offer (Grace) — due 2027-01-14
- Ops: add automated circuit-breaker for queue-depth -> throttle route (Marissa/Infra) — due 2027-01-26

I'll draft an executive brief to send to Atlas and our execs. Good job on the quick mitigations and customer comms.

—Sean
VP, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
